Project: Smart Habitat Occupancy & Crew Safety Tracker
About Us: We are engineering students specializing in digital logic design, embedded systems, and hardware-software integration using ESP32 and sensor arrays.
The Project: Building an automated, reliable entry/exit tracking system to monitor crew movement, maintain habitat safety limits, and manage restricted modules.
Looking For: Teammates skilled in coding, sensor prototyping, and space system design!
summary:
BioSentinel is an offline-first autonomous clinical health monitoring system engineered for astronauts on long-duration exploration missions, such as Mars transit. When interplanetary distances impose communication delays of up to 22 minutes each way, astronauts cannot rely on real-time ground control to diagnose and manage medical crises.

To address this, we developed a system that continuously gathers multi-modal health indicators: real-time biometric vitals (heart rate, HRV, continuous blood pressure, SpO2), environmental life-support telemetry (cabin CO2, radiation dosimeters), and interactive self-assessment tools—specifically an in-browser Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) for cognitive fatigue and an interactive Amsler Grid for Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS).

Using a clinical decision engine aligned with NASA Human Research Program (HRP) thresholds, BioSentinel autonomously evaluates cross-system hazards and prescribes immediate, actionable countermeasures. These include adapted ARED axial-load resistance protocols for bone remodeling, Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) for ocular decompression, solar storm shelter lockdowns, and circadian phototherapy. BioSentinel bridges the gap between deep-space isolation and digital medicine, ensuring crew autonomy and survivability on humanity's journey beyond Earth orbit.
details:
1. How It Works & What It Does

BioSentinel is an offline-first, autonomous digital health system designed to support astronauts on long-duration interplanetary exploration missions (such as Earth-Mars transit). Because deep-space communication delays can reach up to 22 minutes each way, astronauts cannot rely on real-time telemedicine from Mission Control Houston.

BioSentinel operates entirely onboard within the spacecraft’s local network, continuously performing three core functions:

- Multi-Modal Data Ingestion: Gathers continuous physiological telemetry (heart rate, HRV RMSSD, continuous blood pressure, SpO2, core temperature, and sympathovagal stress), environmental life-support sensors (ambient CO2, cabin pressure, and active radiation dosimetry in µGy/hr and cumulative mSv), and daily biochemical markers (urinary NTx for bone resorption and hydration specific gravity).

- Interactive Self-Assessment Suite: Provides astronauts with in-browser diagnostic tools, including a tactile 60-second Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) that quantifies reaction times and attentional lapses (>500 ms) to detect cognitive fatigue, alongside an interactive Amsler Grid canvas to map visual scotomas and globe flattening caused by cephalad fluid shifts.

- Autonomous Clinical Risk Engine: Evaluates cross-system telemetry against NASA Human Research Program (HRP) thresholds, generating holistic health scores and immediate multi-hazard risk categorizations.

2. Benefits & Actionable Countermeasures

Unlike passive telemetry dashboards, BioSentinel immediately closes the loop between diagnosis and treatment. When physiological drift or environmental spikes are identified, the system generates targeted, astronaut-executable countermeasure checklists:

- Bone & Muscle Remodeling: Prescribes adapted axial-load resistance protocols on the Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED)—such as 1.8x Earth bodyweight squats and deadlifts—coupled with calcium and vitamin D3 titration to combat microgravity bone mineral density loss.

- SANS Ocular Decongestion: Detects early optic disc edema and schedules Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) chamber sessions (-25 mmHg) to draw pooled cephalad venous blood back into the lower extremities.

- Radiation Protection: Automatically triggers storm-shelter lockdown protocols and radioprotective antioxidant administration during Solar Particle Events (SPEs).

- Circadian Realignment: Schedules targeted blue-enriched 480 nm phototherapy and micro-rest periods to counteract sleep loss and circadian desynchronization.

3. Creativity & Innovation

- Active Interactive Diagnostics: Rather than relying only on wearable sensors, astronauts actively participate in their health evaluations through gamified, scientifically validated tests (PVT and interactive Amsler eye exams) embedded directly into the flight deck HUD.

- Integrated Mission Crisis Simulator: Includes an onboard scenario injector allowing astronauts (and evaluators) to simulate spaceflight anomalies—such as coronal mass ejections, CO2 scrubber bed saturation, or acute SANS spikes—to verify and rehearse emergency response protocols in real time.

- Hardware-Agnostic Web Audio Alerts: Synthesizes audible aerospace alert chimes natively via the browser's Web Audio API oscillators, eliminating external media dependencies.

4. Factors Considered

- The 5 Hazards of Spaceflight: Structured comprehensively around NASA’s Human Research Program framework: Space Radiation, Altered Gravity, Isolation/Confinement, Hostile Closed Environments, and Distance from Earth.

- Zero-Cloud Resilience: Built with zero external API calls or cloud dependencies, ensuring complete operational reliability in deep-space autonomous isolation.

- Cockpit Ergonomics: Designed with a high-contrast dark flight-ops UI optimized for spacecraft lighting conditions, supporting touchscreens, mouse controls, and tactile keyboard shortcuts.

5. Tools, Languages, & Technologies Used

- Backend: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, NumPy, SciPy, Scikit-learn.

- Persistence: Embedded SQLite for offline time-series biometric logging and clinical audit trails.

- Frontend: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, Chart.js (for high-frequency cardiovascular waveforms), Lucide Icons, and HTML5 Canvas API.

- Version Control: Git and GitHub (open-source MIT License).

6. Intended Impact & Terrestrial Dual-Use

Beyond securing astronaut survival on Artemis and Mars transit missions, BioSentinel offers substantial terrestrial spin-offs. Its lightweight, offline-first autonomous architecture is directly transferable to extreme isolated environments on Earth—including Antarctic research stations, commercial maritime and submarine crews, deep-sea exploration, and remote rural clinics where access to specialized physicians is severely restricted.
